subject: Chains don't move at all for AR(1) model -- please help!!

messages.author: 614b5e0181ba03ae
messages.subject: Chains don't move at all for AR(1) model -- please help!!
parts:
Hi all,
I'm trying to fit a simple AR(1) model as below. But the chains don't move at all. According to the warning message, it suggests to increase adapt_delta. I've made it to 0.999 already but didn't solve the problem. Attached is the trace plot I got...
Please kindly help and feel free to let me know any suggestions that could make the chains move around. Thank you!!

Side note: I'm using
rstan (Version 2.8.0, packaged: 2015-09-19 14:48:38 UTC, GitRev: 05c3d0058b6a)
R version 3.1.2 (2014-10-31) -- "Pumpkin Helmet"
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0 (64-bit)

############ R code starts ############
library(rstan)
A <- 4
B <- 5
N <- A * B
a_n <- rep(1:A, each = B)
b_n <- rep(1:B, times = A)
nu <- 3
rho <- 0.9
sigma_eps <- 0.03
set.seed(1234)
logy <- rnorm(N, mean = 0, sd = 0.05)
y <- exp(logy)
logy_a <- logy[1:A]
X_lower <- log(0.5)
X_upper <- log(2)

test_data <- list(A = A, B = B, N = N,
                  y = y, logy = logy, logy_a = logy_a,
                  nu = nu, rho = rho, sigma_eps = sigma_eps,
                  a_n = a_n, b_n = b_n,
                  X_lower = X_lower, X_upper = X_upper)

test_model3 <- "
data {
int<lower=1> A;
real<lower=0, upper=1> rho;
real<lower=0> sigma_eps;
real logy_a[A];
real X_lower;
real X_upper;
}//end of data

parameters {
real<lower=X_lower, upper=X_upper> X_a[A];
}//end of parameters

model {
real sigmaSQ_eps_stat;
real sigma_eps_stat;

sigmaSQ_eps_stat <- sigma_eps^2 / (1 - rho^2);
sigma_eps_stat <- sqrt(sigmaSQ_eps_stat);

X_a[1] ~ normal(0, sigma_eps_stat) T[X_lower, X_upper];
for (a in 2:A) {
X_a[a] ~ normal(rho * X_a[a-1], sqrt(sigmaSQ_eps_stat * (1 - rho^2))) T[X_lower, X_upper];
}//end of a loop

// data model //
for (a in 1:A) {
logy_a[a] ~ normal(X_a[a], 0.5);
}//end of n loop
}//end of model
"
fit_test3 <- sampling(stan_model(model_code = test_model3),
                      data = test_data,
                      init = 0,
                      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999,#default=0.8
                                     max_treedepth = 12),
                      iter = 2000, chains = 2, warmup = 2)
traceplot(fit_test3, par = dimnames(fit_test3)[[3]][sample(1:dim(fit_test3)[3], size = 5)])

############ R code ends ############

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Chains don't move at all for AR(1) model -- please help!!
parts:
On Tuesday, November 3, 2015 at 9:10:36 AM UTC-5, CFQ wrote:
Please kindly help and feel free to let me know any suggestions that could make the chains move around. Thank you!!

You basically have to Matt trick AR(1) processes for unknown parameters in Stan to get reasonable sampling. Like this:

parameters{
  real Z_a[A];
}
transformed parameters {
  real X_a[A];
  X_a[1] <- X_lower + inv_logit(sigma_eps * Z_a[1]) * (X_upper - X_lower);
  for (i in 2:A) {
    X_a[i] <- X_lower + inv_logit(rho * X_a[i-1] * sigma_eps * Z_a[i]) * (X_upper - X_lower);
  }
}
parameters {
  Z_a ~ normal(0,1);
  logy_a ~ normal(X_a, 0.5);
}

Ben

logy_a <- rnorm(A, mean = 0, sd = 0.05)

The line above is to generate the input data for STAN model.

The line above in STAN is the data model, where I assume that logy_a follows an AR(1). X_a is the parameter vector that I want to estimate. As you mentioned, yes, I didn't generate logy_a by AR(1). I don't see the necessity of generating input data logy_a in R using AR(1) process. Whatever the underlying distribution it has, the chains should at least move around instead of staying at the exact same value.

Regards,
CFQ

On Tue, Nov 3, 2015 at 11:00 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
On Tuesday, November 3, 2015 at 9:10:36 AM UTC-5, CFQ wrote:
Please kindly help and feel free to let me know any suggestions that could make the chains move around. Thank you!!

You basically have to Matt trick AR(1) processes for unknown parameters in Stan to get reasonable sampling. Like this:

parameters{
  real Z_a[A];
}
transformed parameters {
  real X_a[A];
  X_a[1] <- X_lower + inv_logit(sigma_eps * Z_a[1]) * (X_upper - X_lower);
  for (i in 2:A) {
    X_a[i] <- X_lower + inv_logit(rho * X_a[i-1] * sigma_eps * Z_a[i]) * (X_upper - X_lower);
  }
}
parameters {
  Z_a ~ normal(0,1);
  logy_a ~ normal(X_a, 0.5);
}

Ben
